newsitem.title: FINLAND: Sampo hits two-year high on brisk demand.
newsitem.headline: Sampo hits two-year high on brisk demand.

text.p: Shares in Finnish insurer Sampo hit a new two-year high in brisk demand on Friday which followed a recent fall in interest rates and hopes that Merita would be willing to sell some of its insurance holdings, brokers said.
Interest was both domestic and foreign, they said.
At 1525/1225 GMT, Sampo traded at a new two-year high of 315.00 markka, up 11.00 markka or almost four percent. Trade was a lively 44 million markka.
"There has been increasing interest in insurers recently," one broker said. A recent fall in interest rates is expected to boost insurers' investment income, he said.

Another broker said a story in daily Helsingin Sanomat which said there were rumours that Merita group might be willing to reduce its holdings in insurance groups Pohjola or Sampo, may have supported Sampo.
Pohjola also rose, adding 1.40 markka to 85.00 in fair trade.
At end-1995, Merita group including its pension funds held 27.4 percent of Pohjola's votes and 15.9 percent of its shares and 18.2 percent of Sampo votes and 18.5 percent of its shares.
